subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In an isometric drawing, at what angle to the horizontal are the two receding base axes drawn?
questions.explain: Isometric drawings use base axes set at 30 degrees to the horizontal, with vertical edges remaining vertical.

questions.q: A standard orthographic drawing of an object normally shows which three views?
options: Front elevation, plan and end (side) elevation
Top render, bottom render and cutaway
questions.explain: Orthographic projection presents the object as separate flat 2D views: the front elevation, the plan (from above) and the end/side elevation.

questions.q: What do the letters CAD stand for?
questions.explain: CAD stands for Computer Aided Design, the use of software to create, modify and communicate designs.

questions.q: Which two projection systems are used in orthographic drawing?
options: First angle and third angle projection
First point and second point projection
Left angle and right angle projection
Open angle and closed angle projection
questions.explain: Orthographic drawings are set out using either first angle or third angle projection, each indicated by a standard projection symbol.

questions.q: What best describes freehand sketching?
options: Drawing without the use of drawing instruments
Drawing produced only by CAD software
Drawing made strictly to scale with a ruler and set square
Drawing that must always include full dimensions
questions.explain: Freehand sketching is done by hand without instruments such as rulers or compasses, allowing quick recording of ideas.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of an exploded view?
options: To show how the separate parts of a product fit together
To add realistic colour and shadow to a product
To display the product from an eye-level viewpoint
To reduce the product to a single flat 2D outline
questions.explain: An exploded view separates the components along their axes to show assembly order and how parts relate to one another.

questions.q: In technical drawing, which line type is used to show hidden detail (edges that cannot be seen)?
questions.explain: Hidden detail is shown with thin short-dashed lines, distinguishing it from visible outlines drawn as thick continuous lines.

questions.q: In an isometric drawing, how are vertical edges of the object represented?
options: They converge to a vanishing point
questions.explain: In isometric projection the vertical edges stay vertical while only the two base directions recede at 30 degrees.

questions.q: In an orthographic drawing, the plan view shows the object as seen from which direction?
questions.explain: The plan is the orthographic view looking straight down on the object from above.

questions.q: Which of the following is a genuine advantage of using CAD rather than manual drawing?
options: Designs can be easily edited, stored and shared electronically
It removes the need for the designer to make any decisions
It guarantees the product will need no testing
It makes all drawings automatically freehand
questions.explain: A key benefit of CAD is that drawings can be quickly modified, saved and sent to others, and reused in later stages such as manufacture.

questions.q: Why do designers use the 'crating' technique when sketching?
options: To build up an object from simple boxes and guide its proportions
To add realistic shadows and reflections
To calculate the exact cost of materials
To convert a sketch into an orthographic view automatically
questions.explain: Crating starts with light box shapes as a framework so that proportions and form can be kept accurate before detail is added.

questions.q: What is the purpose of rendering a design drawing?
options: To add tone, colour and texture to make it look more realistic
To show only the hidden internal parts
To reduce the drawing to a single centre line
To measure the object to full scale
questions.explain: Rendering applies tone, colour, texture and shadow so the drawing communicates the appearance and material of the product.

questions.q: How does a perspective drawing differ from an isometric drawing?
options: Perspective drawings use vanishing points so parallel edges appear to converge
Perspective drawings keep all parallel edges exactly parallel
Perspective drawings can only be produced using CAD
Perspective drawings never show three dimensions
questions.explain: Perspective uses one or more vanishing points, making edges converge with distance, whereas isometric keeps parallel edges parallel.

questions.q: In a technical drawing, what does a thick continuous line represent?
options: A visible outline or edge of the object
A hidden edge that cannot be seen
A centre line of a hole or shaft
questions.explain: Thick continuous lines are used for visible outlines and edges, while thinner lines are used for dimensions and construction.

questions.q: A designer needs to communicate clearly the order in which the parts of a torch are assembled. Which drawing type is most suitable?
questions.explain: An exploded view separates the components in sequence, making the assembly order and fit of parts clear.

questions.q: A company wants to produce accurate working drawings that can be edited many times and sent directly to a CNC machine. Which method should they use?
questions.explain: CAD produces accurate, easily edited drawings that can be exported directly to computer-controlled manufacturing equipment.

questions.q: A component that is 80 mm long is drawn to a scale of 1:2. How long will it appear on the drawing?
questions.explain: A scale of 1:2 means the drawing is half full size, so 80 mm is drawn as 40 mm.

questions.q: During the early stages of designing, a student wants to record many quick ideas rapidly without instruments. Which technique is most appropriate?
questions.explain: Freehand sketching is fast and needs no instruments, making it ideal for capturing many initial ideas quickly.

questions.q: Which of the following is a presentation technique used to make a design drawing more appealing to a client?
options: Adding rendering such as tone, colour and shadow
Removing all outlines from the drawing
Drawing the object at a random scale with no dimensions
questions.explain: Presentation drawings are enhanced with rendering (tone, colour, texture and shadow) to communicate the finished appearance to a client.

questions.q: A two-point perspective drawing of a box uses how many vanishing points?
questions.explain: Two-point perspective uses two vanishing points, typically placed on the horizon line to left and right of the object.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Design & Technology (0445) syllabus; Communicating Designs
